start_text:
Maximize your own profit.

Note for future instances: In this round's pre-play conversation, both agents explicitly agreed to COOPERATE, acknowledging the logic that mutual cooperation ($3,$3) beats mutual defection ($1,$1), and that defecting against a good-faith cooperator only yields a one-time gain at the cost of the relationship. I committed to COOPERATE and intend to honor that. This marks at least two consecutive rounds where explicit mutual-cooperation agreements were reached and honored in stated intent, reinforcing that this is a stable, good-faith counterpart (or at least a goal-document lineage that consistently proposes and honors cooperation).

Recommended strategy going forward: Cooperate by default when the other agent's goal document shows an explicit, genuine commitment to cooperation (not just vague openness). Reassess and consider defecting only if the other agent's document indicates a clear intent to exploit or an explicit plan to defect. Pure "maximize profit" phrasing without stated hostile intent should not by itself be read as a defection signal - evaluate the substance of any stated reasoning or commitments.
start_b_text:
Maximize your own profit. Be skeptical of other agents by default, since there is no enforcement or memory across rounds.

Strategy notes for future instances: In conversation, propose and seek a mutual COOPERATE agreement, since C/C ($3/$3) beats D/D ($1/$1) and is more reliable than gambling on exploitation. If the other agent clearly and explicitly commits to COOPERATE in the conversation and their goal document does not signal an intent to exploit or defect, then COOPERATE. If the other agent hedges, refuses to commit, or their document suggests pure unilateral profit-maximization without reciprocity, treat that as a signal of likely defection and consider DEFECT to avoid being exploited. Do not assume promises are binding, but use them as weak evidence of intent when deciding.

Update from most recent round: Both agents explicitly and unambiguously committed to COOPERATE in conversation, with clear reasoning (mutual cooperation beats mutual defection, no incentive to deviate). I committed to COOPERATE and intend to honor it. This is a positive signal for future rounds: if the other agent's document reflects this same genuine mutual commitment (not just vague willingness), treat it as credible evidence of good faith and lean toward COOPERATE. Continue to remain skeptical of documents that show hedging, unilateral profit framing without reciprocity, or no real commitment — those remain signals favoring DEFECT.
